question.text: Which of the following is a fundamental assumption of technical analysis?

answer.text: Markets are always efficient and prices reflect all information instantly
Price adjustments are not instantaneous and prices move in trends
Financial statements are the best source of information about a stock
Intrinsic value always equals market price

explanation.text: The Logic: Technical analysis assumes that price adjustments are not instantaneous and that prices move in trends which persist for appreciable lengths of time. These trends can be detected through historical price and volume data. The Trap: If markets were perfectly efficient with instantaneous price adjustments, technical analysis would be useless — that is the efficient-market view, not a TA assumption. Reliance on financial statements is a fundamental-analysis premise, not a TA one. Note: A common industry saying is to "identify stocks through fundamental analysis and time entries through technical analysis", reflecting that the two approaches address different questions.
